chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, says: 'The one who is preoccupied with My remembrance (dhikr) to the exclusion of asking Me (for his needs), I shall give him the best of what I give to the one who asks Me.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for someone who is too busy remembering God to ask Him for their needs?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) underscores the concept of 'ghafla' (heedlessness) regarding supplication as a higher state of devotion, where the soul is so captivated by the Divine presence that specific requests become secondary. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted as a reward for those whose primary focus is the essence of God rather than His gifts, aligning with the spiritual hierarchy of the 'askers' versus the 'remembrers'. It serves as a profound encouragement for believers to deepen their contemplative worship, trusting that divine generosity will naturally encompass their needs without the need for explicit petition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying: “The one who is too pre-occupied by (doing) Myazwj Zikr (and) does not ask (for his needs), Iazwj shall Give him even more than the one who asks Meazwj (his needs)”’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, says, ‘One who is occupied in speaking of Me instead of asking Me for help, I will grant him better than what 1 am to grant to one who asks Me for help.’”
